clue.text: Leading actor honoured — a formality

parts.note: the leading actor in a production is its star
CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour, so someone honoured may carry those letters

explanation.surface: A star of the stage receives an honour, though it is a mere formality.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, an order awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch is figurative stiffness of manner, rigid ceremony and formality.

clue.text: Wisdom I discovered in South American coppers

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found sitting inside it, so one letter goes within the others

parts.note: pennies are copper coins, so coppers are pence

explanation.surface: Someone finds wisdom among South American policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' reads as police, but here it means copper coins, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapience is a literary word for deep knowledge and sagacity.

clue.text: Object to topping part of speech

definitions.meaning: a thing or item, as in an ... of clothing
the word class of 'a' and 'the', which stand at the head of a noun phrase

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a word sitting on top of the others in a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link here; the definite or indefinite word comes first in its phrase, so it tops it.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is both a single item and the grammatical class holding 'a', 'an' and 'the'.

clue.text: A new chair adapted for the use of diners

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh chair is modified so that people at dinner can sit on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges the letters of A NEW CHAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Plates and dishes made of porcelain are what diners eat from at the table.

clue.text: Friendly note in a message

indicators.note: the word in puts the note within the other pieces

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire
MI is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A kindly note is tucked inside a message.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes good-natured, peaceable relations.

clue.text: Union attendant holding up a train

definitions.text: Union attendant holding up a train

parts.words: Union attendant holding up a train
parts.note: reads like a trade union official delaying a railway train, but describes a married woman who carries a bride's gown at a wedding

explanation.surface: A union official stops a railway train in its tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is a marriage and the 'train' is the trailing part of a bridal gown, which she holds up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the married counterpart of the chief bridesmaid at a wedding.

clue.text: Company of soldiers swallow the foreign fish

indicators.note: one piece swallowing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: Coy is the military abbreviation for a company of soldiers
le is French for the, so the in a foreign language

explanation.surface: A unit of soldiers eats a foreign fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coley is a North Atlantic food fish, also called saithe or coalfish.

clue.text: It has endless teeth, as musicians discovered

parts.note: a group of musicians is a band
to have discovered something is to have seen it

explanation.surface: Musicians find something with countless teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' is literal: this tool's blade is a continuous loop of toothed steel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw cuts with a toothed steel loop running round wheels, so its teeth never come to an end.

clue.text: Poe's characters? Shakespeare's corporal? Little Dorrit, for one

indicators.note: the characters, meaning letters, of the name Poe are taken and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
Corporal Nym is a soldier in Shakespeare's Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: A literary quiz runs through Poe's characters, a Shakespearean corporal and Dickens's heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like fictional people but means letters, mixed into EPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Dorrit is a Dickens novel named after its heroine, a person whose name gives a title.

clue.text: Cinema attendant gets percentage on "The Sound of Music"

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits after it

parts.note: a commission is a percentage paid on a sale

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is heard spoken, so a word said aloud gives the spelling

parts.note: an air is a tune, a piece of music

explanation.surface: A cinema usher is paid a cut on a famous musical film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound of Music' looks like the film title; it means the spoken sound of AIR, spelt AIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissionaire is a uniformed doorman at a cinema, hotel or theatre.

clue.text: This garment a favourite with Cato? It could be

parts.note: a pet is a favourite person, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: says the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Would the Roman Cato have loved this item of clothing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges CATO IT into TICOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a woman's underskirt.

clue.text: Jargon used by many in turn

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Specialist talk used by lots of people taking turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Using a Roman numeral for 'many' is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for the specialised vocabulary of a trade or group.

clue.text: Former spouse with right to make an outcry?

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
a claim is a right or title to something

explanation.surface: An ex-partner uses a legal entitlement to raise a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly in surprise or protest.

clue.text: Old journeyman's story

parts.note: reads as a tale from a veteran tradesman, but means the epic of an ancient traveller, Homer's wandering Greek hero

explanation.surface: A veteran tradesman tells his tale.
explanation.walkthrough: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman, but here it is a man on a journey, Homer's hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Greek hero's ten-year voyage home from Troy.

clue.text: In logic he lacked a disciple

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the words logic he lacked

explanation.surface: A follower's reasoning was faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Chela is a Hindi word for a pupil of a guru.

clue.text: Work as guide in Ulster, causing a confrontation

parts.note: to show someone round is to act as their guide
Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland, in the province of Ulster

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job as a tour guide in Northern Ireland and causes a clash.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland, part of the old province of Ulster.
explanation.definitionFit: A showdown is a final decisive clash between opponents.

clue.text: Society girl's television rise? A poet's written about it

indicators.note: the poet's name is written around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Dante is the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises reads upwards, so it is backwards

parts.note: the tube is slang for television

explanation.surface: A young socialite makes her TV debut and a poet writes about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'television rise' looks like a TV debut, but 'rise' turns the screen word upwards to EBUT, which 'written about' encloses in the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young upper-class woman making her first appearance in society.

clue.text: Wine, or posh food, upset daughter in New York

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
grub is slang for food

indicators.note: in puts one piece within the other

explanation.surface: Fancy food spills and a daughter in Manhattan reaches for the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the posh food upwards to BURGU in this down clue; the 'or' between wine and food is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgundy is a wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: See Birkenhead shiver convulsively — he's so ill

parts.note: F.E. Smith, the politician and lawyer, became Lord Birkenhead

indicators.note: shaking in convulsions jumbles the letters of shiver

explanation.surface: Watch Birkenhead shaking with sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town, but here it is F.E. Smith, Earl of Birkenhead; 'convulsively' rearranges SHIVER. 'See' and 'he's so' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone running a high temperature is unwell.

clue.text: Issue half of them — a neat arrangement

indicators.note: half of the word them gives its last two letters
an arrangement of the words a neat puts their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Distributing half of something in a tidy fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or originate from a source.

clue.text: Sail back with ring and aristocratic jewel

indicators.note: back means the word for sail is read backwards

parts.note: a jib is a triangular sail
O is ring-shaped
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: A yachtsman sails back with a ring and a noble's gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijou is French for a jewel or trinket.

clue.text: Little woman in the German legal union

parts.note: Jo March is a heroine of Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A small woman in Germany enters a legal partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' points to Alcott's novel Little Women, not a short woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Joinder is a legal term for joining parties or causes in one action.

clue.text: An outstanding replacement for old watch

definitions.meaning: a sculpted figure standing out from its background
the fresh guard who takes over from the sentries going off duty

explanation.surface: A fine new watch to replace an old timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' suggests a timepiece, but it is a spell of sentry duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A carving raised from its surface stands proud; a fresh crew taking over a shift likewise shares this name.

clue.text: Rejected outcry about state's prevarication

indicators.note: about puts one piece around the other
something rejected is thrown back, so the word for outcry runs backwards

parts.note: an outcry is a loud noise
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: Refusing to answer an outcry about the state is just dodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the noise backwards to ESION, and 'about' wraps that around the state abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is the dodging of a direct answer, as is prevarication.

clue.text: Initially it's lost if anyone cuts this artery

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each word from it's to cuts

explanation.surface: Warning that blood will be lost if anyone severs this artery.
explanation.definitionFit: The iliac arteries supply blood to the pelvis and legs.

clue.text: What the unscrupulous stop at in bagatelle

definitions.meaning: the unscrupulous are said to stop at no limit at all
a trifle, something of no importance

explanation.surface: Ruthless players cheat at a pub board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagatelle' looks like the board game, but it means a trifle; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthless people will stop at zero; a bagatelle is a mere trifle of no account.

clue.text: First question put by republicans to an Arab

indicators.note: the first piece is put beside the other pieces, placed after them

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army
I is the Roman numeral one, meaning first

explanation.surface: Republicans put their first question to an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: I stands for one, the first; 'put by' places it after IRA and Q.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, an Arab country.

clue.text: Dinosaur's droppings in one river

indicators.note: in puts the droppings inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the Don is a river in Russia and in England
guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats

explanation.surface: A dinosaur leaves its dung in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguanodon was a large plant-eating dinosaur.

clue.text: One expects quarrels in this dramatist's work

definitions.text: One expects quarrels in this dramatist's work

parts.words: One expects quarrels in this dramatist's work
parts.note: reads as a remark about conflict in a playwright's drama, but quarrels are crossbow bolts and the work is making arrows, which shares a name with a Jacobean playwright

explanation.surface: Plays by this writer are always full of arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is a crossbow bolt; the arrow-maker's trade name is also that of John Fletcher, Shakespeare's collaborator.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher was a Jacobean playwright, and a fletcher is a maker of arrows.

clue.text: Girl 'with fish to sell down the river

parts.note: Bet is a pet form of the girl's name Elizabeth
a ray is a flat sea fish

explanation.surface: A girl with fish for sale heads down the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone down the river is to double-cross them, an idiom for treachery.
